liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Deal** (2 reviews): Deal closing the first set is singled out as a red-hot highlight; Reviewer points to Deal as worth hearing [9][10]
- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 review): Reviewer points to Brown Eyed Women as worth hearing [10]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer objects to a separate 'jam' track splitting Scarlet Begonias from Fire on the Mountain [15]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): Bobby's Lost Sailor improvisation stands out, as he was still working out the lyrics [17]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 other source): A repeated section of about five seconds was removed [3]

## Setlist highlights

- **Bobby & Drums Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-10-04.sbd.seaweed.bernie-brown.118248.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 184 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: Brent is placed up front in the mix on this soundboard; This soundboard is crisp and up front; Some hiss and minor flaws remain [1][14][20]
- **gd1981-10-04.151473.sbd.hance.sirmick.fixed.flac24**: soundboard; 24 songs; 183 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [3]
- **gd81-10-04.sbd.jim.12887.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 25 songs; 187 min; rated 2.57/5 by 7 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the recording quality excellent, from a tape held over fifteen years; Described as good sound, crisp and high energy, with tight playing; Recording quality is fine, but the pitch runs so flat that it distracts [9][10][11][12]
- **gd1981-10-04.sbd.128620.MrBill.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 185 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [2]

## Around the show

- Bobby told a joke at the start while the crew fixed technical problems; he stayed chatty all night [12]
- Bobby seemed unusually spunky all night, perhaps because of the opening joke [17]
- Reviewer ranks it among the finest shows of 1981 [14]
- Reviewer finds the playing sloppy, preferring a cooler, more fluid approach over fast, fiery playing [18]
- The other soundboard source sounds distant and tinny by comparison [20]
- Unlike the 12887 version, it avoids heavy-handed noise reduction and pitch problems [1]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-10-04.sbd.seaweed.bernie-brown.118248.flac1644**: taped by Seaweed1010 and Bernoe Brown; transferred by AndrewF; source: Source: SBD > ? > Cassette, kindly provided by Seaweed1010 & Bernie Brown. [1]. Also: Same root source as ID-12887, with the same cuts and tape flips; roughly third or fourth generation [1]
- **gd1981-10-04.151473.sbd.hance.sirmick.fixed.flac24**: transferred by John Hance and SIRMick; source: Source: Soundboard Cassette (1st gen) [3]. Also: Tape flips were patched from shnid 127286; the last flip uses an unknown audience source; First notes of Cold Rain and Snow were patched from shnid 28620; John Hance supplied the source and transfer [3]
- **gd81-10-04.sbd.jim.12887.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd1981-10-04.sbd.128620.MrBill.flac16**: transferred by Bill Guarneri; source: Sbd > CM? > C > C; C > Pioneer deck > wav > Sound Forge 10 > TLH > Flac; Could be CM > C. This is one gen (or more) upgrade of shnid 12887 [2]
